headline: Tools derive splicing events, annotation and isoform regulation from transcript-level RNA-seq
label: Isoform Resolved Transcriptome Tooling
summary: New tools turn transcript sets and long-read data into splicing events, annotations and isoform atlases, while Ribo-seq and bacterial RNA-seq are repurposed for termini.
synthesis: The common thread is resolving transcript-level structure and carrying it into downstream interpretation. splicelogic converts transcript-set differences into discrete splicing events, and SQANTI-evidence annotates unannotated genomes from long-read RNA-seq using SQANTI3-curated isoforms plus AUGUSTUS predictions. MOCHI applies a reference-independent k-mer framework to short-read data to curate candidate independent intronic transcripts. scSpAS integrates single-cell and spatial isoform regulation (ATS, splicing, APA, full-length isoforms) across 123 human and other datasets. A commentary on repurposed public bacterial RNA-seq highlights 3' termini mapping as a resource. Edi-Set-Flow (differential A-to-I editing), TISCA2/IncepTIS (translation initiation sites), and Ribotools/Rp-Bp (Ribo-seq with RNA-seq) are adjacent, extending transcript-feature resolution to editing and translation rather than isoform structure itself.
